portInfo.description: Cherbourg’s deep-water harbour and transatlantic history are part of the destination, not just transport infrastructure. The former maritime station now frames both cruise reception and Cité de la Mer, while the town offers art, military history and an active harbourfront. Normandy’s larger historic sites are separate excursions; being in Cherbourg does not make every D-Day beach a nearby walking stop.

climate.rainySeason: Year-round with higher precipitation in autumn

politics.visaRequirements: Entry and visa rules depend on nationality. Many visitors use Schengen short-stay rules, but requirements change—confirm with official government sources and your cruise line before travel.
politics.entryRequirements: Carry a valid passport (or a national ID where your cruise line and destination authorities accept it). Cruise transit formalities can differ from a normal airport entry—follow your ship’s document list.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Cité de la Mer, Former transatlantic maritime station, Quai de France, Cherbourg-en-Cotentin: A substantial maritime/science visit close to cruise reception. Allow about 180 minutes (editorial estimate). Public ticket/entry is separate; submarine sections may have stairs or access restrictions.

Thomas Henry Museum, Musée Thomas Henry, central Cherbourg-en-Cotentin: A city-centre art collection provides a distinct alternative to maritime history. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Check the actual public entrance/opening day before leaving the station.

Musée de la Libération at Fort du Roule, Fort du Roule, Cherbourg-en-Cotentin: Connect the port’s wartime role with the hilltop setting and harbour view. Allow about 120 minutes (editorial estimate). Uphill approach; museum admission and road access need checking.

Port Chantereyne harbour walk, Port Chantereyne, Cherbourg-en-Cotentin: A named marina-side outdoor route shown on the official visitor map. Allow about 60 minutes (editorial estimate). Not the cruise berth; stay on public routes.

Château des Ravalet park, Château des Ravalet, Tourlaville, Cherbourg-en-Cotentin: A park-led alternative outside the immediate port core. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Separate road transfer; do not promise château interior access from a general tourism mention.
